headline: QA-focused digest: agentic UI demos, coverage-as-code, CI protections, mobile testability, and LLM evaluation practices

top_signal.title: Junie adds /demo mode — agentic UI demos with video, report, and CI integration
top_signal.summary: JetBrains’ Junie CLI introduced /demo: an agent mode that builds, launches, and interacts with apps using Computer Use-capable models, producing video, screenshots and an HTML report that can be stored as CI artifacts.
top_signal.why_it_matters: Lets QA delegate routine UI smoke checks to an agent while keeping inspectable evidence (video/report) for reviewers and CI smoke tests.

items.title: Manage 'Restrict code coverage' via REST API — automate coverage gates
items.summary: GitHub’s Changelog: the REST API now supports the 'Restrict code coverage' ruleset option so teams can programmatically create, read and update minimum coverage or maximum drop conditions for PRs.
items.why_it_matters: Enables enforcing coverage-based quality gates at scale via infra-as-code and pipeline automation, improving consistency across many repositories.

items.title: Workflow execution protections for Actions generally available
items.summary: GitHub made workflow execution protections generally available, letting organizations define allowlists to control who or what events can trigger Actions workflows.
items.why_it_matters: QA teams can restrict who triggers expensive or release-scoped test suites, reducing accidental or malicious workflow runs and improving test-run predictability.

items.title: Stage-only npm tokens for safer automation
items.summary: GitHub adds 'Read and write (stage only)' for npm granular access tokens so automation can stage package versions for review without full publish privileges.
items.why_it_matters: Reduces credential blast radius for build and release automation used in test pipelines and package-based smoke tests, improving safety of automation credentials.

items.title: AndroidX Security State Libraries — standardized device security signals
items.summary: AndroidX Security State Libraries expose device security state (patch level, update availability, security fixes) through a consistent API for apps and OEMs to surface device condition.
items.why_it_matters: Mobile QA can programmatically filter devices and target tests based on concrete security-patch and update states, improving test coverage for security-dependent behaviors.

watch.title: Ubuntu 26 runner image for GitHub Actions now GA — validate CI images
watch.summary: Ubuntu 26.04 runner image for GitHub Actions is generally available for x64 and arm64; GitHub provides migration guidance for workflows and runners.
watch.why_it_matters: Runner image changes can alter toolchains, libraries, and test behavior — QA teams should run canary pipelines and validate tests before broad migration.

learning.title: Android Bench 2.0 — benchmark methodology for evaluating LLMs on long‑horizon Android tasks
learning.summary: Android Bench 2.0 extends its benchmark with long‑horizon developer tasks (dependency updates, multi-step builds, feature additions) and model cards to surface strengths and failure modes for LLMs and agents.
learning.why_it_matters: Use its scenario design and model-card approach as a template for robust LLM evaluation when validating AI assistants or agentic QA tools used in development and testing workflows.
